messages:
eve_customer: Hey team — after we moved our inference workload to a Dedicated pool this morning we're seeing a spike in 429s and a big tail on token latency. Started around 08:10 UTC. Low traffic replicate: ~20 rps but many long-context requests (50k tokens).

alice_cs: Sorry to hear that, @eve_customer. Can you paste a sample request + response and the customer project id? Also which model variant are you using?

eve_customer: project: acct-777, model: gpt-large-ctx-32k (redwood/rlm_gpt_large_v2). Sample curl below, response is 429 with body: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' \\  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\  -d '{"model":"gpt-large-ctx-32k","input":"<very long prompt>...","max_tokens":512}'
```

Response: 
```json
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"request throttled due to cache pressure"}
```

bob_sre: tagging in. Seeing similar for another tenant on same Dedicated pool. Early look at runtime metrics: big KV cache eviction spikes coincident with 429s. Memory fragmentation also up. Looks like long-context KV growth + frequent new contexts causing eviction thrash.

carol_ml: That model keeps a big KV per request for 32k contexts. If requests vary a lot, KV cache can't reuse prefixes and you get churn. Do you have many unique conversation IDs?

eve_customer: yes — each user session creates unique conversation id, we also use per-request system prompts (~1k tokens each). The workload is very bursty.

alice_cs: OK. Short-term mitigations we can try: reduce max_context_slice for clients, set client-side prefix caching, or temporarily pin to a smaller context model. Do you want us to apply a quick config to limit per-tenant KV footprint?

eve_customer: please. Any way to avoid a restart? Production traffic critical.

bob_sre: We can apply a throttling rule to this tenant to keep KV allocations below X GB per instance and enable more aggressive LRU eviction for their pool. That should avoid full thrash without node restarts. Rolling change to pool config, no restart required.

dave_eng: From runtime side, there's a known pathological eviction loop with interleaved tiny/big contexts — we landed a mitigation in branch reduce-evict-thrash but it's not deployed to Dedicated yet. Workaround: set "kv_cache_capacity_mb": 2048 (down) and "kv_eviction_policy": "aggressive_lru" for tenant config. Example patch: 

```json
{
  "tenant": "acct-777",
  "kv_cache_capacity_mb": 2048,
  "kv_eviction_policy": "aggressive_lru",
  "soft_limit_pct": 0.75
}
```

bob_sre: Applying those to pool-3 now for acct-777. Monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421-KVTHRASH for pool-3, severity P2. Link: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-0421-KVTHRASH

carol_ml: Also suggestion: enable per-session KV-prefixing (we can shard by user and keep short-term prefix cache). Might reduce unique KV keys. We'll open a ticket for a client SDK change.

eve_customer: thanks. After the change we still saw occasional 429s but tail latency dropped a lot. Any data we can provide to help root cause?

bob_sre: Can you capture one of the affected request IDs (x-rw-request-id header) next time it happens and paste here. Also export runtime metrics for kv_cache_evictions/sec, kv_active_entries, and rss fragmentation around the incident.

eve_customer: will do. We captured request id rw_49a2c3b6. Here's the server log snippet around that id: 

```
[2026-04-21T08:22:14Z] rw_49a2c3b6 INFO alloc_kv size=24576kb tenant=acct-777
[2026-04-21T08:22:14Z] rw_49a2c3b6 WARN evict_start entries=512 target_free=12000kb
[2026-04-21T08:22:14Z] rw_49a2c3b6 ERROR throttle_trigger reason=kv_memory_pressure
[2026-04-21T08:22:14Z] rw_49a2c3b6 INFO responded 429 latency_ms=4200
```

bob_sre: exactly the pattern. Eviction starts then immediate throttle. Next steps: 1) keep aggressive_lru for acct-777 2) schedule Dedicated pool scaling to add +2 GPUs to pool-3 for the next 24h 3) deploy reduce-evict-thrash patch to Dedicated runtime in canary.

dave_eng: I'll open a PR for the runtime fix and a canary deploy plan. ETA for canary: 2 business days.

alice_cs: I'll follow up with the customer on the short-term config change and scaling. @eve_customer we'll also send a small SDK snippet to reduce unique conversation ids.

eve_customer: appreciated. Please keep me posted. :thumbsup:

bob_sre: Closing out for now, monitoring dashboard shows evictions/sec down 80% and 429s trending to zero after config + scale. Will re-open if anything recurs.
